pr.title: Fix for async drop inside async gen fn
pr.description:
<!-- homu-ignore:start -->
<!--
    https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/126482
    r? oli-obk
-->
<!-- homu-ignore:end -->

Return value (for yield) is corrected for async drop inside async gen function.
In CFG, when internal async drop future is polled and returned `Poll<()>::Pending`, then async gen resume function returns `Poll<(OptRet)>::Pending`.

Fixes rust-lang/rust#140530
pr.author: azhogin

analysis.summary: In the coroutine drop expansion (expand_async_drops), the synthetic yield emitted when an internal async-drop future returns Pending was hard-coded to the boolean constant `false`. That is valid for ordinary gen/return-yield situations but wrong for AsyncGen coroutines, whose yield type is `Poll<Option<T>>`. The fix constructs an unevaluated `AsyncGenPending` constant of the full yield type when the coroutine is an async generator, preventing malformed MIR (`Assign((_0, const false))` with mismatched types) and the associated ICE.
analysis.originalLogic: When expand_async_drops creates the callback/return path after polling an internal async-drop future, it always built the yielded value as a single shared constant: `// value needed only for return-yields or gen-coroutines, so just const here` followed by a `ConstOperand` using `const_: Const::from_bool(tcx, false)`. This single `false` value was then used for all coroutine kinds.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: For an async generator (`CoroutineKind::Desugared(CoroutineDesugaring::AsyncGen, _)`), the drop-expansion pass used the generic boolean `false` as the value of the pending yield. Because an async generator's yield type is `Poll<Option<T>>`, this transformed a yield/return into `Assign((_0, const false))` where `_0` has type `std::task::Poll<std::option::Option<()>>` but the right-hand side has type `bool`, i.e. the historical wrong rewrite inserted a bool constant where a `Poll<Option<T>>::Pending` value was required. The corrected transformation instead builds an unevaluated constant for the `AsyncGenPending` lang item with the yield type: `Const::Unevaluated(UnevaluatedConst::new(tcx.require_lang_item(LangItem::AsyncGenPending, None), tcx.mk_args(&[yield_ty.into()])), full_yield_ty)`.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust 2024-edition async generator functions that use async drop, enabled by `#![feature(async_drop, gen_blocks)]`; the minimal historical input is `async gen fn a() { _ = async {} }`. More generally, any async gen body where async-drop expansion polls an internal async drop future and handles its `Poll<()>::Pending` result by yielding to the caller.
analysis.trigger: An async generator contains an async drop operation whose internal future is polled and returns `Poll<()>::Pending`. The drop-expansion logic then needs to return `Poll<OptRet>::Pending` from the async gen resume function instead of yielding the generic `false` value.
preconditions: The compiler is lowering a coroutine with async drops via `expand_async_drops`.
An async drop future poll yields `Poll<()>::Pending`, so the drop expansion inserts a yield/return path.
The async gen yield type is `Poll<Option<T>>`, so the pending value must be `AsyncGenPending` rather than a plain bool.
pitfalls: Do not use a constant of type bool for a coroutine yield place whose type is `Poll<Option<T>>`; MIR validation rejects the incompatible assignment.

The generic `false` constant is only appropriate for return-yields or non-async-generator gen coroutines; async generators require the `AsyncGenPending` lang item with the concrete yield type as a generic argument.

When destructuring the full yield type, both the outer `Poll` and the inner `Option` ADTs are assumed; preserving the actual element type via `args.type_at(0)` is necessary for the `AsyncGenPending` constant.
A retained test name or old `known-bug` comment is not evidence of correctness; the actual assignment types in the decoded MIR must be compared.
analysis.testStrategy: Convert the crash reproducer into a UI build-pass regression test under `tests/ui/async-await/async-drop/` (the PR renames `tests/crashes/140530.rs` to `tests/ui/async-await/async-drop/assign-incompatible-types.rs` and changes `//@ known-bug: #140530` to `// ex-ice: #140530` plus `//@ build-pass`). Keep `//@ edition: 2024`, `#![feature(async_drop, gen_blocks)]`, and `#![allow(incomplete_features)]`, with a minimal `async gen fn a() { _ = async {} }`. This ensures MIR validation of the async gen coroutine (after drop elaboration/optimization) does not encounter an `Assign` of bool into `Poll<Option<T>>`. Focus the test on async-gen plus async-drop lowering rather than on unrelated generic coroutine behavior.
